info.title: DOE IRA Rebate API
info.description:
API for processing rebates under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). Client software can connect to the API at https://sandbox-test.ira-rebates.labworks.org/.

### Swagger JSON
The original swagger json is at https://sandbox-test.ira-rebates.labworks.org/api-doc/swagger

### About the beta v4 releases
The IRA Rebate API dev team is completing the work of updating the system to match the Data and Tools Guide v1.2 and finalizing all endpoints for the real-time processing of rebates (reservations and redemptions). As significant portions of the update are completed, they will be made available to API users for testing here.

### Release 2025-01-08
- **Fixed contractor_dac_incentive field validation**: An issue where users were unable to create a DIY reservation in a DAC due to contractor_dac_incentive validation issues. A contractor_dac_incentive is NOT required when a reservation is DIY in a DAC.
- **User specifiable reservation_amount**: Users can now also specify a reservation amount. The user-specified amount will be applied to the reservation if it is lower than the API calculated reservation amount. This is to allow fine management of reservation for upgrade_types that allow multiple reservations.
- **Support for multiple reservations for specific 50122 upgrade_types**: Multiple concurrent reservations can now be created for the following upgrade types: ELECTRICAL_PANEL, ELECTRIC_WIRING, and INSULATION_AIR_SEALING_VENTILATION. The maximum rebate amounts still apply for these upgrades. 
- **ahri_reference_number update**: JSON Schema has been updated to accept AHRI numbers that are 9 digits.

### Release 2024-12-13
- **Added num_occupied_units field**: A new field named `num_occupied_units` has been added for reservations where `building_project_type` is `MULTIFAMILY_CENTRAL` or `MULTIFAMILY_IN_UNIT_PART_OF_BUILDING_PROJECT`. This field is currently optional, but will be made required at a later date.

### Release 2024-12-06
- **Bug Fix for project_id field**: A string type project_id field was being incorrectly rejected, saying it needed to be a UUID. That is no longer the case.
- **Formatted Swagger JSON for Download**: The Swagger JSON file available on the documentation page has been updated to a "pretty format" for improved readability and usability when downloaded.
- **Required `dwelling_unit_income_bucket` for MULTIFAMILY_IN_UNIT**: A bug has been fixed where now the `dwelling_unit_income_bucket` field is required in rebate API for the `MULTIFAMILY_IN_UNIT` building project type.
- **Bug Fix for rounding energy savings when applying rules**. A hotfix has been implemented correctly round the internally calculated energy savings used when determining reservation amount.


### Release 2024-12-02
- **DAC Incentive Requirement for Homes and Electrification Reservations**: The `contractor_dac_incentive` field is now required for reservations in disadvantaged communities (DAC) across real-time and reporting APIs. DAC determination prioritizes user-provided status over address-service responses.
- **RFC3339 Validation for `purchase_date_time`**: Both the bulk reporting and real-time redemption endpoints now validate `purchase_date_time` fields to ensure compliance with the RFC3339 date-time standard. Empty strings are no longer allowed.
- **New `purchase_date` Field**: A `purchase_date` field has been introduced alongside `purchase_date_time` for creating product redemptions. Validation ensures mutual exclusivity between these fields for backward compatibility. The `purchase_date_time` field is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Users are encouraged to adopt `purchase_date` as soon as possible.
- **Corrected Validation for `multipleOf` Fields**: Fixed an issue where fields with a `multipleOf` constraint in the JSON schema could fail validation even when valid decimal values were provided.
- **Extend Reservation Endpoint**: Added new endpoints to extend reservation expiration dates:
  - `PUT /electric/{reservation_id}/extend`
  - `PUT /homes/{reservation_id}/extend`
  Reservations with redemptions or those that have expired cannot be extended.

### Release 2024-11-01
- **Enhanced JSON Schema Error Reporting for Reporting API**: The reporting API now validates all elements of the reporting array for JSON schema errors, providing grouped error reporting for each array element instead of just the first identified error.
- **Contractor DAC Incentive Field for Homes Reservations**: The `contractor_dac_incentive` field is now available in both real-time and reporting APIs for creating homes reservations.
- **UI Updates - Rebate Details**: Users can now view rebate details directly from within the dashboard.
- **Breaking Change - Safety Check Fields Update**: Updated JSON schema for safety_check fields, which now require values of `YES`, `NO`, or `NA` instead of booleans. Note: This change is not backward-compatible.
- **Modeled Savings Calculation Adjustment**: For Homes reservations, the energy savings calculation have been revised to round 19.5% to 20%.

### Release 2024-10-11
- **Bulk Rebate Reporting**: New endpoints have been added for bulk rebate reporting in the Electrification and HOMES programs.
- **Electrical Panel Upgrade**: The component details for Electrification upgrades involving an electrical panel now support a minimum value of 30 amps.
- **Reservation Deletion**: A new `delete_redemptions` option (default: `false`) has been added to the reservation deletion endpoints. When set to `true`, this option allows associated redemptions to be deleted along with the reservation. If set to `false`, reservations with associated redemptions cannot be deleted.
- **Maximum Rebate for Specific Upgrades**: Electrification reservations for HEAT_PUMP_CLOTHES_DRYER and ELECTRIC_COOKING_APPLIANCE upgrades now each qualify for a maximum rebate of $840. These amounts are no longer combined for these two upgrade types.
- **HOMES Redemptions**: Redemptions for HOMES now allow a value of $0 for the `equipment_and_material_cost` field.
- **Limited Assessment**: A limited assessment can now be provided for any Electrification upgrade. It is required for HEAT_PUMP_FOR_SPACE_HEATING_OR_COOLING and optional for all other Electrification upgrades.


### Release beta v4.2 (8/7/2024)
This release includes
- A new endpoint POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/limited-assessments
- A new endpoint POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/state-addenda
- A new endpoint POST /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/state-addenda
- Added contractor_dac_incentive and contractor_incentive fields in the payload for /electric/reservations
- An added safety_checks field (itself an object) in the payloads for POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/install-redemptions and POST /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/redemptions
- Including state, county, city, and zip_code in any response that includes the address_id
- Email addresses must conform to the https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5322 spec
- The HPXML file_type used in POST /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/files has been split into HPXML_MODELED_RECOMMENDED, HPXML_MODELED_REQUIRED, and HPXML_MEASURED to match the options in the Data and Tools Guide v1.2 Table 9
- Relaxed the requirements on the street_number field used in the POST /address-service/addresses endpoint
- The installation_cost field is now a number (instead of an integer) with up to two places after the decimal allowed
- An added reservation_amount field is now required in the payload for POST /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/redemptions in the MEASURED savings case
- A warning message is included in the response under the following circumstances:
  - When making a MEASURED 50121 reservation if there is a completed 50122 reservation in the sytem for the same household or building
  - When making a MODELED 50121 reservation if there is a 50122 reservation in the system (open or completed) for the same household or building
  - When making a MODELED 50121 redemption if the reported rebate_deducted does not match the expected rebate amount
  - When making a 50122 reservation if there is an open MODELED 50121 reeration for the same household or building
  - When making a 50122 product or install redemption if the reported rebate_deducted does not match the expected rebate amount
- You may notice small changes to the rules applied to reservations and redemptions, however, a complete set of rules will be applied in a subsequent release, so we do not suggest focusing on the rules too seriously until that release.
- Updated JSON Schema files for all POST and DELETE endpoint payloads will be posted at https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API in the https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/tree/beta_v4_schema branch

### Feedback needed
For this release, please focus on the new endpoints and the changes to the JSON Schema. Please test all endpoints to verify that they perform as indicated by the documentation. Please try out sequences of reservations and redemptions at the same address.


### Release beta v4.1 (7/17/2024)
This release includes
- Endpoints to support redemption creation, retrieval, and deletion for Homes (50121) and Electrification (50122) rebates
- A new `POST /applicants` endpoint for generating a unique applicant identifier from an applicant's last name, email address, and phone number
- New `POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/files` and `POST /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/files` endpoints for associating files with a reservation


### Release beta v4.0 (6/25/2024)
This release includes
- JSON Schema files are available at https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/tree/beta_v4_schema which are used by this API to validate the POST and DELETE endpoint payloads. These files provide precise descriptions of required data fields and can be an aid to users developing their client code. As a further aid to users, the folder https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/tree/beta_v4_schema/resolved_json_schemas now contains json schema files with all internal references resolved. A user can use these resolved json schema files together with an online json schema validator to troubleshoot validation errors during development.
- Users have access to a dashboard that provides  real-time metrics for the rebate data the user is authorized to see.
- The `POST /address-service/addresses` endpoint converts a building address into a unique address ID.
- Endpoints to support reservation creation, retrieval, and deletion for Homes (50121) and Electrification (50122) rebates.
- An authentication system is being used. (See the "Authentication" section below.)
- Rules have been implemented that will reject reservation requests based on existing or previous reservations at the same address. (See the "Rebate Rules" section below.)

### Authentication
- The authentication protocol for this API is based on OAuth 2.0.
- You must log in to the system using your username and password. The first time you do this, you will be prompted to set up two-factor authentication.
- Once you are logged in, you can obtain an authentication token by navigating to the Settings page.
- To use the "Try it out" button for any endpoint in this Swagger document, you must first use the "Authorize" button (with the lock icon) and enter your authentication token prepended with the word Bearer.
- To connect to the API from your client software, you will need to use a JWT Bearer token provided by the front-end GUI (obtainable at `/dashboard/settings`).
- Currently, the authentication token will expire after 24 hours.

### Rebate Rules
The complete set of rebate rules will be included in a subsequent release.

### Reservation amount for measured HOMES
The states that implement the measured option of the HOMES rebate program will specify how the reservation amount should be calculated. In lieu of that information, beta v4.0 of the API sets the reservation amount to $6000 per dwelling unit for <80%AMI and $3000 per dwelling unit for 80%AMI and higher.

### Typical API workflow for Electrification (50122)
- Obtain `address_id` from `POST /address-service/addresses`
- Obtain `applicant_id` from `POST /applicants`
- Create a reservation using `POST /electric/reservations`
	- Obtain `reservation_id` from the response
- Submit a product redemption using `POST  /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/product-redemptions`
- Submit a limited assessment as needed using `POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/limited-assessments`
- Submit Quality Installation documentation as needed using `POST  /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/files`
- Submit an install redemption using `POST  /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/install-redemptions`

### Typical API workflow for HOMES (50121)
- Obtain `address_id` from `POST /address-service/addresses`
- Obtain `applicant_id` from `POST /applicants`
- Create a reservation using `POST /homes/reservations`
	- Obtain `reservation_id` from the response
- Submit modeling data files (HPXML, ...) as needed using `POST  /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/files`
- Submit a state attestation that any failed inspection items have been remediated using `POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/state-addenda`
- Submit quality installation documentation as needed using `POST  /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/files`
- Submit a redemption using `POST  /homes/reservations/{reservation_id}/redemptions`
- Submit the amount the state paid to the rebate claimant using `POST /electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/state-addenda`

post.description:
This endpoint processes a building address and returns the following information:
• a unique address_id
• 80% and 150% Area Median Income (AMI) dollar amounts for household sizes ranging from one to eight
• the Disadvantaged Community (DAC) status for the location
• and a validity score from 0 to 1 indicating the likelihood that the given address is valid. 

 If the score is below 0.80, the address will be rejected. A score between 0.80 and less than 0.90 will trigger a warning. API users are responsible for validating and normalizing the address. Note that a GUID will not be created if a street name or number cannot be resolved. The API will reject an address if the AMI or is_disadvantaged_community values cannot be determined. 

 For detailed information on the possible combinations of required fields, refer to the schema documentation at: https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/blob/main/json_schemas/addressServicePayload.schema.json. In the context of multifamily buildings, this should be the building's address and not an individual unit. Other API endpoints will require a unit number or name as needed.

get.description: This endpoint takes the address_id obtained from a previous call to /address-service/addresses and returns the same data returned from that endpoint.

post.description: Given an applicant's email address, phone number, and last name, this endpoint will return a UUIDv4 applicant identifier. The last name field and at least one of the email address or phone number fields is required. To specify that a field is not available, please provide the string 'NOT AVAILABLE'. The applicant identifier will be unique and consistent for the same combination of email address, phone number, and last name.

post.summary: Refresh JWT token using refresh token
post.description: This endpoint refreshes the JWT token using the provided refresh token. It sends a POST request to the token endpoint with the refresh token. If successful, it returns a new JWT token. If the refresh token is invalid or expired, an error message is returned.

Use this endpoint to bulk upload rebate information for reporting purposes. The entire upload will be rejected if any of the rebates fail data validation.Note: this endpoint is separate from the reservation and redemption endpoints. See the 'Reporting endpoints vs Reservation & Redemption endpoints' section at the top of this document for a description of the two options.

400.description: Invalid File (or) Invalid data in uploaded file

post.summary: Report the rebate reservations created offline
post.description: Use this endpoint to report rebate reservations using a JSON file. Reservations will be created if the data meets the specifications outlined in the JSON Schema.The file will not be processed in cases where a reservation with identical data already exists, or if any data validation failures occur.

400.description: Invalid File (or) Invalid data in uploaded file

get.description: Retrieve all electrification rebate reservations that the current API user is authorized to access. The resulting list can be filtered using query string parameters. For example, `/electric/reservations?upgrade_type=HEAT_PUMP_WATER_HEATER&building_project_type=MANUFACTURED`, will restrict the list to reservations for heat pump water heaters in manufactured homes.

post.summary: Create a reservation for an electrification rebate
post.description:
Create a separate reservation for each upgrade type. For example, a heat pump water heater and a stove top to be installed in the same dwelling unit will require separate reservations for each. However, insulation, calk for air sealing, and an exhaust fan are all in the same *upgrade_type*, so only one reservation is needed if they are to be installed in the same dwelling unit. Similarly, separate reservations are required for an upgrade to be installed in multiple units in a multifamily building. This allows the system to track which units are getting the upgrade and the pre-upgrade details for each unit. However, a whole building upgrade for a multifamily building such as a shared heat pump water heater, requires only one reservation.

See https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/blob/main/json_schemas/electricReservationsPayload.schema.json for a precise description of when fields are required under different rebate scenarios.

get.summary: Get an electrification rebate reservation by ID
get.description: Retrieve a detailed view of a reservation by reservation ID. This will include a detailed list of all redemptions associated with the reservation.

delete.description: This will mark a reservation as canceled.

200.description: Reservation and any associated redemption are deleted successfully

put.summary: Extend the expiration date for a homes rebate.
put.description: Use this endpoint to extend the expiration date for a homes rebate. New date must be in a format of YYYY-MM-DD.

400.description: Bad request in case of invalid input

post.description: This endpoint can be used to attach a file to a reservation. Quality assurance documentation is the primary use case. Please notify the API development team if you need an additional file type to be added to the list.

Use this endpoint to submit a redemption for the installation of a qualified product. See https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/blob/beta_v4_schema/resolved_json_schemas/electricInstallRedemptionsPayload.schema.json(https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/blob/beta_v4_schema/resolved_json_schemas/electricInstallRedemptionsPayload.schema.json) for further details regarding specific fields.

equipment_and_material_cost.description: This should not include the cost of the qualifying product(s) for this rebate. Those should be provided using the `/electric/reservations/{reservation_id}/product-redemptions` endpoint. Include incidental equipment and materials costs directly related to installation here.

rebate_deducted.description: This is the amount that was deducted from the applicant's (homeowner, building owner, renter) invoiced amount for the installation.

ProductInfo.description: Provide identifying information for the qualifying product or products that are covered by this rebate.

address_id.description: A unique identifier associated with the address of the building at which the upgrade(s) will be installed. This id must be obtained using the address-service endpoint.
address_id.title: Address id

ahri_reference_number.title: AHRI reference number
ahri_reference_number.description: The AHRA Reference Number associated with a heat pump or heat pump water heater. See the AHRI Directory of Certified Product Performance at  https://www.ahridirectory.org/Search/SearchHome?ReturnUrl=%2f for more information regarding AHRI Reference Numbers.

applicant_id.description: This identifier is unique to the applicant (the building owner or renter that is to benefit from the rebate). It must be obtained from the API /applicant endpoint.
applicant_id.title: Applicant id

binary_file_content_base_64.description: The API user must convert the binary file content to base64 encoding.
binary_file_content_base_64.title: Binary file content Base64

claimant_payment.description: This is the amount that the state paid to an aggregator, or other claimant, for a HOMES rebate.
claimant_payment.title: Claimant payment

construction_type.title: Construction type
construction_type.description: Set to NEW if the building is less than one year old. Otherwise, set to EXISTING.

contractor_company_name.title: Contractor company name
contractor_company_name.description: The name of the primary contracting company for the project.

contractor_dac_incentive.description: This is the amount the state will pay to a contractor as a disadvantaged-community incentive. This field is required if the address of the building is within a DAC.
contractor_dac_incentive.title: Contractor DAC incentive

contractor_incentive.description: This is the amount the state will pay to a contractor as an incentive. This is separate from any contractor DAC incentive.
contractor_incentive.title: Contractor incentive

contractor_name.title: Contractor name
contractor_name.description: The name of the primary contractor for the project.

count.title: Count
count.description: This should be set to 1 in most cases. An example of a situation where a value greater than 1 is appropriate is when several rolls of insulation are being purchased. Another situation is for `building_project_type` MULTIFAMILY_CENTRAL and `upgrade_type` HEAT_PUMP_WATER_HEATER for which the shared water heating system upgrade consists of multiple identical heat pump water heaters.

deletion_reason.title: Deletion reason
deletion_reason.description: Provide a reason for deleting the reservation. CANCEL_RESERVATION indicates that the intention is to delete the reservation with no immediate intention of replacing it. CORRECT_RESERVATION indicates that the intention is to delete the reservation in order to replace it with another.

delete_redemptions.title: Delete redemptions
delete_redemptions.description: A boolean flag to determine if the redemption(s) for this reservation will be deleted. When this flag is set to true, any associated redemption for the reservation will also be deleted.

doe_approved_bpi_2400_compliant_software.title: DOE approved bpi 2400 compliant software used
doe_approved_bpi_2400_compliant_software.description: This field is required when *rebate_type* is MODELED. Otherwise, this field should be omitted. A list of approved software will be publicly available along with the corresponding string that should be used here. We use a string rather than an enum because the approved list may change often.

electric_building_project_type.title: Building project type
electric_building_project_type.description: This describes both the type of the building and, in the multifamily case, whether the upgrade in this reservation applies to the whole building or to a single unit. If it applies to a single unit, there is a further distinction between an upgrade that is part of a whole building project and a stand-alone upgrade. For the MULTIFAMILY_IN_UNIT_PART_OF_BUILDING_PROJECT and MULTIFAMILY_CENTRAL cases, the income bucket for the building, mf_income_bucket, is used. Otherwise, the income bucket for the dwelling unit, dwelling_unit_income_bucket, is used.

electric_claimant_type.title: Claimant type
electric_claimant_type.description: The type of person or entity that is initiating the rebate process on behalf of the applicant.

electric_dwelling_unit_income_bucket.title: Dwelling unit income bucket
electric_dwelling_unit_income_bucket.description: The household income level of the applicant compared to the area median income (AMI).

electric_equipment_and_material_cost.title: Equipment and material cost
electric_equipment_and_material_cost.description: The total cost of the equipment and materials purchased as part of a redemption.

electric_install_redemptions_equipment_a.title: Equipment and material cost
electric_install_redemptions_equipment_a.description: The total cost of the equipment and materials purchased as part of a redemption.

electric_install_redemptions_installatio.description: The installation costs associated with this redemption. To qualify, the installation must be performed by an approved contractor. Also see `is_contractor_eligible`.
electric_install_redemptions_installatio.title: Installation cost

electric_mf_building_income_bucket.title: Multifamily building income bucket
electric_mf_building_income_bucket.description: Choose the lowest area median income (AMI) range for which at least 50% of the household units fall into the range or lower. For example, consider a five-unit apartment building for which one units falls in the `LESS_THAN_80%_AMI` range, two fall in the `80%_AND_GREATER_BUT_LESS_THAN_150%_AMI`, and the other two have household incomes above these ranges. Then the `80%_AND_GREATER_BUT_LESS_THAN_150%_AMI` range should be chosen because more than half of the units fall into this range or lower.

electric_reservation_amount.title: Requested reservation amount
electric_reservation_amount.description: Optional API user-specified reservation amount. Use this to request a reservation amount that is less than the otherwise allowed amount. For example, this can be helpful if you need several concurrent reservations to support different parts of a project and need to make sure the total of the reservations will not exceed the $14,000 household cap.

energy_data_evaluation_permission.description: Set to true if the home/building owner has given their permission to share energy data with the State and the DOE for evaluation purposes.
energy_data_evaluation_permission.title: Energy data evaluation permission

estimated_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh.title: Estimated post retrofit energy usage kwh equivalent
estimated_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh.description: The total estimated (expected) annual  energy usage converted to kWh-equivalent for the home or multifamily building post-retrofit. This field is used for MEASURED reservations only.

external_rebate_id.title: External rebate id
external_rebate_id.description: This is an optional field that a state can use for their own purposes to identify a rebate or rebate reservation.

file_name.description: This file name will be associated with the uploaded file and will be shown wherever a list of the uploaded files for a reservation is returned.
file_name.title: File name

homes_building_project_type.title: Building project type
homes_building_project_type.description: This describes both the type of the building and, in the multifamily case, whether this reservation applies to the whole building or to a single unit. For the MULTIFAMILY_CENTRAL case, the income bucket for the building, mf_income_bucket, is used. Otherwise, the income bucket for the dwelling unit, dwelling_unit_income_bucket, is used.

homes_claimant_type.title: Claimant type
homes_claimant_type.description: The type of person or entity that is initiating the rebate process on behalf of the applicant.

homes_dwelling_unit_income_bucket.title: Dwelling unit income bucket
homes_dwelling_unit_income_bucket.description: The household income level of the applicant compared to the area median income (AMI).

homes_equipment_and_material_cost.title: Equipment and material cost
homes_equipment_and_material_cost.description: The total cost of the equipment and materials purchased as part of a redemption.

homes_mf_building_income_bucket.title: Multifamily building income bucket
homes_mf_building_income_bucket.description: Choose the lowest area median income (AMI) range for which at least 50% of the household units fall into the range or lower. For example, consider a five-unit apartment building for which two units fall in the `LESS_THAN_80%_AMI` range and three fall in the `80%_AMI_AND_GREATER`. Then the `80%_AMI_AND_GREATER` range should be chosen because more than half of the units fall into this range or lower.

homes_reservation_amount.title: Measured reservation amount
homes_reservation_amount.description: The API user-specified reservation amount for a MEASURED rebate. This field is required for rebate_type MEASURED and otherwise not allowed. The API does not calculate a reservation amount in the MEASURED case. The value provided here will be reserved in the system for the rebate.

homes_upgrades.title: Homes upgrades
homes_upgrades.description: List all the upgrades from the enumeration that apply to the HOMES project.

installation_cost.description: The installation costs associated with this redemption. To qualify, the installation must be performed by an approved contractor. Also see `is_contractor_eligible`.
installation_cost.title: Installation cost

is_contractor_eligible.description: The contractor is eligible if they are on the state's approved list.
is_contractor_eligible.title: Is contractor eligible

is_disadvantaged_community.description: This field should only be used by states that have been approved by the DOE to do so. If provided, this will override the is_disadvantaged_community value from the address-service.
is_disadvantaged_community.title: Is disadvantaged community

is_final_project_redemption.description: Set this to true if the project work has been completed and there will be no more redemptions made on this reservation. This will, among other things, free up any remaining reservation amount for the household's future use.
is_final_project_redemption.title: Is final project redemption

measured_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_.title: Measured post retrofit energy usage kwh equivalent
measured_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_.description: The total actual annual energy usage converted to kWh-equivalent for the home or multifamily building post-retrofit - based on normalized utility bill data. This field is used for MEASURED redemptions only.

measured_pre_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_e.title: Measured pre-retrofit energy usage kwh equivalent
measured_pre_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_e.description: The total actual annual energy usage converted to kWh-equivalent for the home or multifamily building prior to the retrofit - based on normalized utility bill data. This field is used for MEASURED reservations only.

mf_conditioned_floor_area.title: Multifamily conditioned floor area
mf_conditioned_floor_area.description: The conditioned floor area for the entire multifamily building including common areas.

mf_num_bedrooms.title: Multifamily num bedrooms
mf_num_bedrooms.description: The number of bedrooms for the entire multifamily building.

model_number.title: Model number
model_number.description: The model number for the product being purchased.

modeled_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_e.title: Modeled post retrofit energy usage kwh equivalent
modeled_post_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_e.description: The total annual modeled energy usage converted to kWh-equivalent for the home or multifamily building post-retrofit. This field is used for MODELED reservations only.

modeled_pre_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_eq.title: Modeled pre energy usage kwh equivalent
modeled_pre_retrofit_energy_usage_kwh_eq.description: The total annual modeled energy usage converted to kWh-equivalent for the home or multifamily building as-found (prior to the retrofit). This field is used for MODELED reservations only.

new_expiration_date.title: New expiration date
new_expiration_date.description: The new date at which the reservation should be set to expire.

num_occupied_units.title: Num occupied units
num_occupied_units.description: This is the number of occupied units in a multifamily building.

num_units.title: Num units
num_units.description: This is the total number of units in a multifamily building. This field is required when *building_project_type* is any of the enumerated values that has a "MULTIFAMILY" prefix. Otherwise, the field should be omitted.

num_units_meeting_income_bucket.title: Num units meeting income bucket
num_units_meeting_income_bucket.description: This is the number of occupied units in a multifamily building for which the household income falls within the income range represented by *mf_income_bucket* or is lower.

original_component_details.title: original component details
original_component_details.description: This object describes the details of the component being replaced. The required fields depend on the upgrade_type and are fully described at https://github.com/pnnl/IRA-Rebates-API/blob/main/json_schemas/electricEligibleRebatesPayload.schema.json.

percent_cost_limit.description: This integer is either 50 or 100 (for electrification) or 50 or 80 (for homes), depending on the income_bucket. It is the percent of project cost that can be covered by the rebate. The actual rebate amount allowed is *min(reservation_amount, percent_cost_limit x project_cost / 100)*.
percent_cost_limit.title: Percent cost limit

vendor_percent_cost_limit.description: This integer is either 50 or 100 (for electrification) or 50 or 80 (for homes), depending on the income_bucket. It is the percent of project cost that can be covered by the rebate. The actual rebate amount allowed is *min(reservation_amount, percent_cost_limit x project_cost / 100)*.
vendor_percent_cost_limit.title: Percent cost limit

portfolio_id.description: Multiple reservations for MEASURED HOMES projects can be tied together into a portfolio by assigning the same portfolio_id value to each reservation in the portfolio.
portfolio_id.title: Portfolio id

product_description.title: Product description
product_description.description: The description of the product being purchased, as it would appear on an invoice.

product_info.description: Provide identifying information for the qualifying product or products that are covered by this rebate.

project_completion_date.title: Project completion date
project_completion_date.description: This is a calendar date in the form YYYY-MM-DD. Time zone is immaterial.

project_id.description: This is a unique string supplied by the API user that is used to associate one or more reservations to a single project. Note: it is recommended that a uuid be used to avoid duplication, but the API user can use any other system that they find convenient, provided that it is unique for the state.
project_id.title: Project id

purchase_date.title: Purchase date
purchase_date.description: This is a calendar date in the form YYYY-MM-DD. Time zone is immaterial. This represents the date the product was purchased. Either this field or 'purchase_date_time' is required for product redemption.

purchase_date_time.title: Purchase date-time
purchase_date_time.description: This is the date and time a product was purchased. Either this field or the 'purchase_date' field is required for product redemption. Note that the 'purchase_date_time' field will be deprecated in the future.

rebate_deducted.title: Rebate deducted
rebate_deducted.description: This is the amount that was deducted from the customer's/homeowner's purchase price or invoiced amount for products and/or installation.

rebate_passed_through_to_applicant.title: Rebate passed through to applicant
rebate_passed_through_to_applicant.description: Use this field when the contractor submitted a product redemption for this reservation and received a rebate on behalf of the applicant. Otherwise set this to 0. This amount must be passed on to the applicant and shown on the invoice. Do not include this in the amount for `equipment_and_material_cost`.

rebate_type.title: Rebate type
rebate_type.description: The HOMES rebates have two distinct options for determining savings and rebate amounts, MODELED vs MEASURED.

remaining_reservation_amount.description: This is the maximum rebate amount. The rebate amount is also limited to a percentage of the project cost which is given by the *percent_cost_limit* field. Thus, the rebate amount is the smaller of the *reservation_amount* and the percent of the project cost, given by *percent_cost_limit*.
remaining_reservation_amount.title: Remaining reservation amount

redemption_notes.description: This will be an array of strings explaining how the rebate_amount was calculated.

reservation_amount_note.description: This is an array of strings explaining how the reservation amount was determined.

reservation_expiration_date_time.description: If the reservation is not redeemed by this date, the reservation will be automatically canceled.

sf_conditioned_floor_area.title: Single-family conditioned floor area
sf_conditioned_floor_area.description: This is the conditioned floor area for an individual dwelling unit, either a single-family home or a unit in a multifamily building.

sf_num_bedrooms.title: Single-family num bedrooms
sf_num_bedrooms.description: The number of bedrooms in the dwelling unit.

software_used_to_estimate_post_retrofit_.title: Software used to estimate measured savings
software_used_to_estimate_post_retrofit_.description: This field is required when `rebate_type` is `MEASURED`.

state_attests_proof_of_identity_ownershi.title: State attests proof of identity ownership income
state_attests_proof_of_identity_ownershi.description: The state attests that they have obtained the required proof of identify, proof of ownership, and proof of income for this rebate.

state_attests_any_failed_inspection_reme.title: State attests any failed inspection remediated

unit_name_or_number.title: Unit name or number
unit_name_or_number.description: This is the unit designator for a unit in a multifamily building. Do NOT include words or abbreviations such as 'APT' or 'UNIT'. For example, if the unit is referred to as 'APT 7B', then *unit_name_or_number* should be '7B'.

upc.title: UPC
upc.description: The universal product code (UPC) for the product being purchased.

upgrade_component_details.title: Upgrade component details
upgrade_component_details.description: This is a JSON object containing the upgrade information specific to the upgrade being installed. The form of these objects will follow the Data and Tools Guide Appendix https://www.energy.gov/scep/articles/ira-home-energy-rebates-data-and-tools-requirements-guide  and will be fully documented here in the next release version.

upgrade_type.title: Upgrade type
upgrade_type.description: The upgrade covered by this reservation. These upgrade types are the ones specifically listed in the IRA legislation.

upgrade_subtype.title: Upgrade suptype
upgrade_subtype.description: The use of this field is state-specific. A state could base a rebate rule on this field value.

vendor_coupon_id.title: Vendor coupon id
vendor_coupon_id.description: The unique identifier for the vendor coupon.

vendor_id.title: Vendor id
vendor_id.description: This is a unique identifier for a vendor that the state will reimburse in connection with a redemption.

street.title: Street
street.description: The name of the street, avenue, etc.. This would be “Horn Rapids Road” for the address: 650 Horn Rapids Road, Richland, WA 99354.

street_number.title: Street number
street_number.description: The building number. This would be “650” for the address: 650 Horn Rapids Road, Richland, WA 99354.

email.description: The email address of the homeowner, building owner, or renter that will ultimately be receiving the benefit of the rebate.

phone.description: The ten-digit phone number of the home owner, building owner, or renter that will ultimately be receiving the benefit of the rebate.

created_at.title: Created at
created_at.description: This is the date and time, in UTC, at which the redemption was created.

Is percent conditioned floor area served known
